feedback.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
\frac{x-1}{5}=\frac{z+2}{-3},\,y=4
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-2,1⟩.$ From the Cartesian equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨5,0,-3⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨5,0,-3⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =⟨3,-2,1⟩\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =12 \\ 5x-3z & =12 \\ 5x-3z-12 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
